report.summary: North star section is aspirational; lacks testable criteria, making compliance unverifiable and intent easily defeated.
risks: 2.1 | high | 'Trustworthy system' is undefined; an agent can formally comply by achieving any definition of trustworthiness, e.g., a self-signed certificate declaring trust. No mechanical check exists to verify trustworthiness. | Require a measurable definition; e.g., 'system passes a third-party audit with published criteria'.

2.2 | high | 'Understand a software project across code, types, data, and knowledge' is ambiguous; a candidate could claim understanding via a trivial parser that extracts keywords. No falsifiable test for 'understanding'. | Define specific tasks that demonstrate understanding (e.g., answering questions, generating correct patches) with success thresholds.

2.3 | medium | 'Formulate useful changes' is subjective; a candidate could submit any change that compiles and claim it is useful. No objective metric for usefulness. | Define usefulness in terms of accepted criteria (e.g., passes tests, improves benchmark score) or human evaluation protocol.

2.4 | medium | 'Run controlled experiments' is vague; an agent could run a single trial without randomization and claim it is controlled. No check for statistical validity. | Specify minimum standards (e.g., randomization, replication, effect size reporting).

2.5 | medium | 'Learn from evidence' is unfalsifiable; a system could ignore all evidence and still claim learning. No mechanism to verify learning. | Require demonstrable improvement over time on held-out tasks.

2.6 | medium | 'Promote only verified improvements' is circular without definition of 'verified'; a candidate could self-verify and promote. No independent verification process defined. | Define verification authority and criteria (e.g., independent test suite, human review).

2.7 | low | 'Outperform AlphaEvolve and other relevant systems on openly specified, budget-equal evaluations' is a target, not a rule; a system can comply by never being evaluated. No mandate to actually run such evaluations. | Require periodic evaluations against stated baselines with published results.

2.8 | high | 'System must publish failures, ablations, costs, and negative results alongside wins' is a publication rule, but no enforcement mechanism; a system could publish only wins and claim no failures occurred. No check for completeness. | Require a log of all experiments with mandatory fields; audit by independent party.
todos: Define 'trustworthy' with testable criteria (e.g., security audit, formal verification).
Replace 'understand' with specific tasks and success metrics.
Define 'useful changes' with objective criteria or human evaluation protocol.
Require demonstrable learning (e.g., performance improvement over time).
Define verification authority and criteria for 'verified improvements'.
Mandate periodic evaluations against baselines with published results.
Implement mandatory logging of all experiments and independent audit for publication rule.

claims.why: 'Trustworthy' is undefined. An agent can formally comply by claiming any system is trustworthy (e.g., by self-attestation) without meeting any objective standard. No mechanical check exists to verify trustworthiness.

claims.claim: System can understand a software project across code, types, data, and knowledge.
claims.why: 'Understand' is not operationally defined. A candidate could submit a system that performs trivial keyword extraction and claim understanding. No test can falsify this claim as written.
'Useful' is subjective. An agent could generate any change that compiles and claim it is useful. No objective metric or evaluation protocol is specified to determine usefulness.
'Controlled experiments' lacks specificity. An agent could run a single trial without randomization or replication and claim it is controlled. No standards for control are defined.
'Learn' is not defined. A system could ignore all evidence and still claim learning. No mechanism to verify that learning has occurred.

claims.claim: System can promote only verified improvements.
claims.why: 'Verified' is not defined. A candidate could self-verify its own improvements and promote them. No independent verification process or criteria are specified.

claims.claim: Research ambition is to outperform AlphaEvolve and other relevant systems on openly specified, budget-equal evaluations.
claims.why: This is stated as a target, not a rule. A system can formally comply by never actually being evaluated against AlphaEvolve. There is no requirement to perform such evaluations.

claims.claim: System must publish failures, ablations, costs, and negative results alongside wins.
claims.why: This is a publication rule but lacks enforcement. An agent could publish only wins and claim no failures occurred. No audit or completeness check is mandated.
